plan: Daily back-to-wall développé and standing-leg wall lift at moderate height
Film one extension from the front at the end of the week and compare it with frame 5
plan.focus: Foundation: feel the straight standing leg and vertical spine

plan: Raise drill heights toward full extension while keeping the knee and spine checks
Add the straight-knee battement path and the straddle-hold knee lock
Arm-anchor balances in retiré, progressing to extension
plan.focus: Strength: hold the posture at higher leg heights

Run the jump-to-landing section with eyes up for 4 counts after each landing
Film a full run; check frames like 5 and 22 against this report

drills.cue: Standing leg grows taller as the high leg goes up.
drills.how: Stand sideways to a wall, inside hand lightly on it. Développé the outside leg to the side as high as she can control it. As the leg rises, press the floor away with the standing foot and think of the top of her head going up. Hold 4 counts, lower slowly, and check the standing knee never bends.
drills.name: Standing-leg wall lift

drills.cue: Ribs over hips, then the leg.
drills.how: Stand with her back, shoulder blades and the back of her head touching a wall. Développé to the side or front only as high as she can go without her shoulders or head leaving the wall. Hold 3 counts, lower over 4.
drills.name: Back-to-wall développé

drills.cue: Long knee the whole way up and down.
drills.how: From fifth, do slow grand battements to the side over 4 counts up and 4 counts down. She keeps the back of the knee long the whole way and lifts from under the thigh instead of kicking from the foot. If the knee bends, lower the height.
drills.name: Straight-knee battement path

drills.cue: The arm holds the shape while the leg works.
drills.how: In retiré on demi-pointe, place her arms in second and hold 8 counts without letting either elbow drop or either arm sink. Then repeat with an extension in place of the retiré. A phone video from the front checks whether the arms match.
drills.dose: 3 × 8-count holds each side, 5 days a week
drills.name: Arm-anchor balance

drills.cue: Land, then look at the back row.
drills.how: Do 4 sautés in first, finishing the last in a held relevé or demi-plié. On landing she picks one fixed spot at eye level across the room and holds her eyes there for 4 counts with the arms held. A parent or friend can call out if her eyes drop.
drills.name: Land-and-look sautés

drills.how: Sit in a straddle on the floor with her back tall. Press the backs of the knees down, point the feet, and lift both heels an inch off the floor for 5 seconds. Release and repeat.
drills.name: Straddle-hold knee lock

report.closing:
Ava, your leg goes higher than most dancers will ever get theirs, and your straddle looks like you're hanging in the air. What's left is the quiet stuff. Let the standing leg grow tall, stay over your hips while the leg goes up, and keep your eyes up after you land. Frame 7 shows you already know how. Now make every frame look like that one.

Coach

fix: Let the eyes find the audience before the first move rather than the floor line
moments.skill: Opening shape, pointe tendu with arms low and open
moments.title: Opening — tendu on pointe
working: Calm, upright posture from the first count
moments.analysis: Knees 178.6° and 179.3°: both legs fully pulled up from the first count. Torso lean is a gentle 5.4°, and her arms are low and soft (22.3° and 32.6°). It is a quiet, confident start that tells the panel this is a classical dancer.

fix: Lift through the ribs here so the lean doesn't build as the leg climbs
moments.skill: Right leg rising to the side at hip height, balance on left
moments.title: Extension begins — leg at hip height
moments.analysis: At 102.1° of lift her standing knee is still locked at 179.7°, the best supporting leg in the phrase. Torso lean is already 10.3°, though. The spine is starting to give way before the leg reaches its peak.

fix: Keep the back of the working knee long the whole way up
Initiate from under the thigh, not a kick from the foot
moments.skill: Right leg passing 156° on the way up
moments.title: Passing through — working knee
moments.analysis: The working knee reads 161.3°, so the leg is bending as it travels up. Torso lean has reached 11°. It is only a fraction of a second, but a panel sees it as the leg being thrown rather than lifted.

fix: Re-lift the left arm to match the right
Grow up through the standing leg
moments.skill: Right leg at 171.1°, approaching the top
moments.title: Nearly vertical — standing leg softens
moments.analysis: The leg is almost vertical, but the standing knee has dropped to 173.5° and torso lean is 12.9°. The left arm has sunk to 27.1° while the right sits at 43°, so the arms no longer match.

fix: Standing knee straight at the peak
Round, lifted left arm instead of a bent drop
moments.title: Développé — the top of the line
moments.analysis: Her best leg in the clip: 173.9° lift and a 171.9° split. The support side pays for it. The standing knee is 169.3°, the standing hip opens to 158.1°, torso lean is 13.1°, and the left elbow bends to 150°. Straighten the standing side and this same leg reads noticeably longer from the judges' table.

fix: Close the last few degrees in the standing knee
moments.skill: Extension held on pointe, arms in high V
moments.title: On pointe — the model frame
moments.analysis: This is the version to copy: leg still at 172°, torso lean down to 5.7°, standing knee 175.5°, and arms lifted to 160.2° and 165.1°. Pulling the arms up lifted her spine with them. Hip height is 0.50, the highest standing reading in the phrase.

fix: Hold the working knee straight on the way down
moments.title: Lowering the leg
moments.analysis: The descent is controlled and the arms open to second (79.9° and 103.2°). The working knee softens to 171.5° and the right elbow to 142.7°. Lowering the leg is judged the same as lifting it.

fix: Check the knees on a side-angle video to see whether they're fully locked in the air
moments.skill: Split jump on the way up
moments.title: Straddle rising
working: Legs above hip line before the apex
moments.analysis: Legs are already above horizontal at 116.8° and 112.2° from vertical, with the torso perfectly upright at -1.6°. The arms are lifted (138.5° and 134.2°) and the feet are pointed. It is a strong, organized take-off.

fix: Squeeze the knees fully straight at the peak
moments.skill: Straddle jump at its highest point
moments.title: Jump apex — suspended straddle
working: No forward lean at the top
moments.analysis: Both legs sit above the hip line (117.5° and 114.7°), hips are at their highest (0.55), and the torso is at -1.2°. Knees read 165.7° and 167.9°. From a front camera, turnout can shorten a knee reading, so confirm from the side. If they really are soft, locking them is the last detail on an already excellent jump.

fix: Keep the face up here; it's about to drop
moments.skill: Finishing the jump in wide second with arms high
moments.title: Landing into open relevé
moments.analysis: Knees 177.8° and 179.1°, torso lean -1.5°, arms held at 117° and 113.9°. She lands, controls it, and keeps the upper body up. Technically this is a clean finish.

fix: Head and eyes up to the audience
Carry the arms higher in the transition
moments.skill: Settling in second after the jump
moments.title: Eyes to the floor
moments.analysis: Legs are fine at 179.1° and 178.4°, but her head is down and her eyes are on the floor. Her arms have dropped to 49.8° and 54.8°. For a moment the dancer disappears, right after her biggest skill.

fix: Nothing major; keep the neck long
moments.skill: Fifth on pointe, arms in second, head turned
moments.title: Sous-sus with épaulement
moments.analysis: A tight sous-sus: knees 176.4° and 176.5°, arms even at 73.7° and 74.7°, torso lean -2.3°, and the head turned to finish the shape. This is the classical polish a panel rewards.

fix: Keep the arms where they were in frame 28 until the music ends
moments.title: Final shape
working: Steady on pointe to the end
Focus held out to the side
moments.analysis: Legs and spine stay solid (torso lean -1°), but her arms have sunk from 73.7°/74.7° in frame 28 to 57.6°/62.1° here. The last picture is the one judges write their final score next to, so hold it at full size.

onStage.cue: Before your first move, find a spot at the back of the room at eye level and breathe out once. Start from there, not from the floor.
onStage.title: Eyes up first

onStage.cue: Before the extension, lift your ribs and grow tall through the standing leg. Only then let the leg go up. Height comes after posture, not instead of it.
onStage.title: Tall before the leg

onStage.cue: Breathe in on the prep. In the air think 'knees long'. When you land, pick a face in the audience and keep looking at it for four counts.
onStage.title: Jump, then hold

onStage.cue: If a balance shifts, keep your face and arms exactly where they were and come down on purpose, like it was choreographed. Judges forgive a wobble way more than a panicked face.
onStage.title: Own the wobble

onStage.cue: Keep your arms at full height in the final pose and count to four after the music stops before you relax.
onStage.title: Hold it longer

onStage.cue: When you walk off, name one thing that felt great and one thing for next time. Then let it go until the next rehearsal.
onStage.title: One good, one next

report.opening:
I watched Ava's eight-second classical pointe phrase frame by frame: the opening tendu, the extension to the side that rises to nearly vertical, the balance on pointe with arms in a high V, the straddle jump, the landing, and the sous-sus finish. This is advanced, competition-level ballet. Her right leg reaches 173.9° from vertical (frame 5). Her split jump shows both legs above the hip line at the top (frame 17). Her feet are fully pointed in every airborne and relevé frame.

Because her level is high, her points will come from the details a top panel separates on. Her supporting knee softens as the leg goes up, from 179.7° in frame 2 to 169.3° in frame 5. Her torso tips further off vertical as the leg climbs. Her eyes drop to the floor after the jump (frame 22). None of these are about flexibility or strength. They are about control and finishing, and they can all be trained in a hallway.

A note on the camera: it sits in front, so the jump and side-extension numbers are 2-D projections. The split and knee readings in the air may read lower than they really are. I say where that applies.

verdict.current: Advanced classical technique that would score in the high range at regional level. Her extension and jump already look like a top-tier dancer's, and the deductions come from the supporting leg, vertical posture under the high leg, and how she finishes after big skills.
verdict.timeline: Three to four focused weeks for the supporting-leg and posture habits. The landing focus can change at her next rehearsal.
verdict.potential: With a locked supporting knee, a vertical spine under the extension, and eyes held up through landings, Ava's phrase reads as clean as it is impressive. That is the difference between a high score and a top overall placement.

glossary.meaning: Unfolding the working leg slowly from the knee into a high, straight extension.
The leg she is standing on. Judges watch that it stays fully straight.
A big, controlled kick of a straight leg, lifted and lowered with control.
A tight fifth position up on pointe, legs crossed and squeezed together.
The angle of head and shoulders that gives classical shapes their finish.
Rising onto demi-pointe or full pointe.
The carriage and movement of the arms.
Feet apart to the side, or arms open out to the sides.
A jump with both legs split out to the sides in the air.

report.headline: Elite extension and a flat split jump; the supporting side is next
forParent: In the car, lead with what she nailed: the height of her leg and that suspended straddle jump.
Don't quote angles at her or point out every frame. Pick one cue a week from the priorities list.
Ask her teacher to watch her standing knee and torso during extensions in class. That's the number-one fix.
If you can, film the jump once from the side so her teacher can check whether her knees are fully straight in the air.
Let the drills be her routine, not your checklist. Ten minutes a day beats an hour on the weekend.

strengths.title: Extension most dancers never reach
strengths.detail: 173.9° of leg lift with a 171.9° split in frame 5, still near 172° on pointe in frame 7. Judges score extension heavily in a classical piece, and hers is in the top bracket.

strengths.title: A straddle that flies flat
strengths.detail: At the apex both legs sit above the hip line (117.5° and 114.7° from vertical), her torso is nearly upright at -1.2°, and her arms are lifted (149° and 144.7°). The jump looks effortless and suspended.

strengths.title: Balanced and upright on pointe at full height
strengths.detail: In frame 7 she holds a 172° extension on pointe with only 5.7° of torso lean and the supporting knee at 175.5°. That shows the posture she needs everywhere else already exists in her body.

strengths.title: Finished feet throughout
strengths.detail: The working foot is pointed at the top of every extension frame, and both feet are fully pointed in the air. She never gives away a cheap foot deduction.

strengths.title: Clean pointe finish
strengths.detail: The sous-sus in frames 28 and 31 shows knees at 176.4° and 176.5°, legs closed tight, and the head turned with épaulement. It is a polished final picture.

categories.name: Lines & extension
categories.summary: Her right leg reaches 173.9° from vertical with a 171.9° split (frame 5), and it holds near 172° on pointe in frame 7. To be excellent rather than very good, her supporting knee needs to stay straight while the leg is at the top.

categories.name: Alignment & core
categories.summary: Torso lean grows from 10.3° (frame 2) to 13.1° (frame 5) as her leg rises, but drops to 5.7° in frame 7. That shows she can stay upright when she organizes for it. Supporting hip and knee give way together in frame 5.

categories.name: Jumps
categories.summary: The straddle peaks with both legs above horizontal (117.5° and 114.7° from vertical, frame 17), torso near upright at -1.2°, and arms in a lifted V. Knee readings of 165.7° and 167.9° in the air should be checked from a side angle. The landing finishes on full extension (frame 20).

categories.name: Turns & balance
categories.summary: No full turn is visible in these frames. The best evidence is frame 7, a high extension held on pointe with the supporting knee at 175.5° and torso lean only 5.7°, which shows real balance control.

categories.name: Arms & port de bras
categories.summary: Arms are long and lifted in frame 7 (160.2° and 165.1°) and in the jump. During the extension the left arm drops and bends: 27.1° lift in frame 4, elbow 150° in frame 5. It stops matching the line her legs are making.

categories.name: Feet & pointe work
categories.summary: The working foot is fully pointed at the top of every extension (frames 3–7) and both feet are finished in the jump (frame 17). Her sous-sus in frames 28–31 is tight and well over the box.

categories.name: Presence
categories.summary: Calm, regal carriage, with the head turned to finish the épaulement (head-and-shoulder angle) in frames 28 and 31. The eyes go to the floor right after the jump (frame 22), and that is the moment the panel notices.

judgesCard.name: Technique
judgesCard.note: Gorgeous extension, really up there. Watch that standing knee though, it's softening as the leg goes up.

judgesCard.name: Execution & precision
judgesCard.note: Lovely feet everywhere. Keep the working knee long on the way up and the way down, not just at the top.

judgesCard.name: Performance quality
judgesCard.note: Beautiful carriage on pointe. Don't look down after that jump, stay with us.

judgesCard.name: Choreography & musicality
judgesCard.note: Smart build from extension to jump to pointe finish. I want to see that balance in the high V really breathe on the music.

judgesCard.name: Presentation
judgesCard.note: Clean, classic look, hair and lines very polished. Hold those arms in the final pose, they're sinking.

judgesCard.name: Overall impression
judgesCard.note: Very talented technician. Finish every shape and this is a top score.

priorities.cue: Standing leg grows taller as the high leg goes up.
priorities.why: Her standing knee reads 179.7° in frame 2, 173.5° in frame 4 and 169.3° in frame 5, so it softens in step with the leg rising. From the judges' table a soft standing leg shortens the whole vertical line and reads as reaching rather than controlling. The cause is effort: she pushes down through the supporting side to get the leg up, instead of lifting out of it.
priorities.title: Keep the supporting knee straight as the working leg goes to the top

priorities.cue: Ribs over hips, then the leg.
priorities.why: Torso lean climbs from 10.3° (frame 2) to 11° (frame 3), 12.9° (frame 4) and 13.1° (frame 5). Her supporting hip also opens, from 168.8° to 158.1°. She is trading spine for leg height. Frame 7 shows she can hold the same extension with only 5.7° of lean when she pulls up first, so this is a habit, not a limit.
priorities.title: Stay vertical under the extension

priorities.cue: Land, then look at the back row.
priorities.why: Frame 20 finishes beautifully with arms lifted, but by frame 22 her head is down and her eyes are on the floor. A panel reads that as relief or self-checking. It costs presentation and performance points right after her most impressive skill.
priorities.title: Keep the eyes up through the jump landing

priorities.cue: Long knee the whole way up and down.
priorities.why: On the way up the right knee reads 161.3° (frame 3), and on the way down it reads 171.5° (frame 9). It is straight only at the top. A judge sees the whole path, not just the peak, and a bent knee on the way up looks like the leg is being thrown.
priorities.title: Keep the working knee straight all the way up the battement

priorities.cue: The arm holds the shape while the leg works.
priorities.why: Her left arm sinks to 27.1° of lift (frame 4) and her left elbow bends to 150° (frame 5) while her legs make a perfect line. The upper body stops matching the lower body, and the shape looks less finished than her legs deserve.
priorities.title: Keep the support-side arm alive during the extension
